Client Consulting & Solution Strategy

• Build credibility and trust through strong consulting, communication, and facilitation skills.

• Act as an advocate for customer success and long-term platform adoption.

Documentation & Operational Excellence

• Maintain accurate project records, workload estimates, and time tracking documentation.

• Create client-facing documentation, presentations, and recommendations using Microsoft Office tools.

• Continuously expand Adobe Workfront expertise through certifications, training, and self-study.

• Stay current on Adobe Workfront product enhancements, features, and industry best practices.

Required Skills & Experience

• Deep technical expertise in Adobe Workfront and Workfront Fusion.

• Strong understanding of Workfront work management capabilities, including resource management, reporting, proofing, and document management features.

• Experience implementing Adobe Workfront within enterprise environments.

• Experience designing and configuring business workflows and project management processes

title: Head of AI Operations
description:
OUR MISSION

We're not your average benefits platform - we're the driving force that uplifts people's lives. Our technology connects the entire benefits ecosystem, creating better outcomes for employers, employees, brokers, and providers.

Our mission is clear: to build a world where everything works at its best, ensuring every employee gets the support they need to thrive-both at work and beyond.

YOUR MISSION

As our Head of AI Operations, you own Ben's internal applied AI transformation: reinventing how the whole company works, function by function, so the business runs on a new operating system. You'll work directly with the founders, with the backing, budget and authority to make it a reality.

It's a once-in-a-lifetime role. Where most people get one team and a backlog, you get the whole company as your canvas, from customer operations to commercial, finance and people. You find the work that's slow, manual and held together with duct tape, and you rebuild it so it runs itself. Piece by piece, that becomes the way Ben operates.

There's no better place to do it. Ben's whole mission is to make things work at their best, and we already do that in benefits for thousands of companies. Now we're doing it to ourselves, and you're the one who leads it.

THINGS YOU'LL BE WORKING ON

- Rebuild the company operating system: partner with customer operations, finance, people and commercial to find what's slow, manual and held together with duct tape, and redesign it so it runs seamlessly.

- Reinvent how work happens: get hands-on with each function to design and stand up the systems that take on whole workflows end to end, then drive them across the company. description:
We are looking for a highly motivated Transportation Sales Executive to help build Spotter's direct-shipper freight pipeline.
This is a hands-on sales role focused on identifying freight opportunities, connecting with shippers and logistics decision-makers, and helping get Spotter's 600-truck fleet into new freight opportunities.
You will work closely with our sales, operations, and pricing teams to identify qualified opportunities and turn them into lanes, bids, pilots, and recurring freight.
Initial Market Focus
This hire will initially focus on local work around Joliet, IL and long-haul freight leaving the Joliet, IL area.
What You'll Do

• Research and identify potential direct shippers with relevant freight volume.

• Build and maintain a pipeline of prospective shippers in the Joliet market.

• Reach out to transportation, logistics, and procurement contacts.

• Identify upcoming RFPs, mini-bids, pilots, and truckload opportunities .

• Help prospective shippers complete carrier onboarding and qualification processes.

• Introduce Spotter's 600-truck capacity to qualified freight opportunities.

• Follow up consistently with prospects and move opportunities toward a concrete next step.

• Work with operations and pricing to determine which lanes Spotter can service and price.

• Maintain accurate pipeline and account information in our CRM.

• Help develop direct-shipper relationships that can grow into recurring freight.

What We're Looking For

• Previous experience in freight sales, transportation, logistics, brokerage, 3PL, or a related field is a plus.

• Strong communication and prospecting skills.

• Comfortable with outbound calls, email outreach, and LinkedIn prospecting.

• Understanding of FTL / truckload transportation is a plus.

• Ability to identify and qualify potential freight opportunities.

• Strong follow-up and organization skills.

• Comfortable using CRM systems and transportation technology.

• Self-motivated and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment.

• Willingness to learn direct-shipper sales and freight procurement .

Experience with shipper RFPs, carrier onboarding, TMS platforms, digital freight platforms, or transportation procurement is a plus.
What Success Looks Like
Success in this role means consistently building a qualified pipeline of direct-shipper opportunities and moving prospects toward carrier onboarding, RFPs, bids, pilots, and awarded lanes.
You will be measured primarily on qualified opportunities and tangible pipeline progress , rather than simply the number of calls or emails completed.
Why Spotter
Spotter operates a 600-truck asset base , giving you the opportunity to sell real transportation capacity and develop direct relationships with shippers.
You'll have the opportunity to learn enterprise freight procurement, direct-shipper sales, and contract truckload , while growing into larger strategic accounts as you demonstrate results.

About Lokal
In 2018, we began with a WhatsApp group with a simple hypothesis: people in tier-2/3 towns weren’t really using the internet meaningfully yet. We believed that if we started with local content in their own language, they’d come back every day; once there was a habit and trust, that same space could naturally grow into classifieds and, eventually, something they used for almost everything online. This spark became Lokal . Our first instinct was to put everything in one place & one app - local updates, classifieds, jobs, matrimony and more. It worked, till it stopped working. Users gave us the insight - when one use case outweighs the others, everything else seems like noise. We listened. Like how Craigslist quietly seeded a generation of focused companies & marketplaces, we began unbundling and verticalising.
Today, Lokal is a house of focused apps, many products, one mission:
to connect Tier-2/3+ India to the Knowledge, opportunities, tools and experts they’ve always deserved.
We now operate dozens of live apps across categories like:

• Edutainment & Skill Learning - practical skills and learning in regional languages (GyanTV)

• Matrimonial Matchmaking - hyperlocal, compatibility-first partner search ( Lokal Matrimony)

• Agri Consulting - farmer-first advisory in local languages (Agri Lokal )

• Local Jobs - blue- and grey-collar opportunities close to home ( Lokal Jobs)

• Social & Community - Place to find & post social updates ( Lokal app)

• Emotional Well-being & Peer Support - safe spaces to talk and feel heard (Dostt & Eaze)

• Astrology & Guidance - instant access to trusted Astrologers via chat and voice (Astro Lokal )

• Advisory Services - early bets in legal help, financial guidance, career counselling, and more

Under the hood, Lokal is a discovery and access platform: local-language internet + deep Bharat insight+ AI. When someone opens a product we’ve built, they don’t wade through clutter; they get a straight line to what they came for.
This is the story new teammates walk into:
a company that started as a whatsapp group, became a family of focused apps, and kept one belief at the centre - access changes lives .

We ship fast. We learn fast. We build for Bharat.
We are backed by leading global and domestic investors including Y Combinator, Sony, Global Brain, India Quotient, and 3one4 Capital.

title: Robotics Navigation and Control Engineer

About Slip Robotics

Slip Robotics is transforming freight logistics with autonomous robotic systems that load and unload trailers faster, safer, and more reliably than traditional methods. Our robots operate in demanding real-world environments alongside people and heavy cargo every day. We are looking for a Robotics Navigation and Control Engineer to own the motion planning, path planning, and control systems on our autonomous mobile robots. Our robots navigate constrained spaces-inside trailers, across loading docks, and through active warehouse floors-carrying heavy loads with tight tolerances. This role is responsible for making that movement safe, precise, and reliable.
We need someone who has shipped navigation and controls software on real robots at real customer sites. You should have hands-on experience tuning controllers on physical hardware, dealing with wheel slip, load dynamics, and the gap between simulation and reality. Academic publications are great, but production deployment experience is what matters here.
Key Responsibilities

• Design, implement, and optimize path planning and trajectory generation for autonomous mobile robots operating in constrained logistics environments

• Develop and tune motion controllers (PID, MPC, or similar) for heavy-payload platforms with real-world dynamics

• Experience with localization techniques (EKF, particle filters, scan matching, visual odometry)

• Demonstrated ability to bridge the sim-to-real gap-tuning algorithms that work on actual hardware, not just in simulation

• Comfort analyzing system behavior from logs and telemetry data

• Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively in a small team

Nice to Have

About WorkOS 🚀

WorkOS builds modern developer tools and APIs that make it easy for companies to become Enterprise Ready. Our platform powers authentication, identity, authorization, and other critical infrastructure that developers need to securely scale their products to large organizations.

We recently raised a $100M Series C, valuing the company at $2B, led by Meritech and Sapphire with participation from Greenoaks, Craft, Abstract, and Audacious. WorkOS powers enterprise features for many of the fastest-growing AI companies, including OpenAI, Cursor, and Perplexity, Sierra, and Plaid.

As AI reshapes software, WorkOS is at the frontier of Human and Agent Authentication, Identity, and Access Control helping companies answer a new critical question: who are your agents, and what are they allowed to do? Our fast-growing customer base includes hundreds of modern software companies building the next generation of enterprise-ready products.

ABOUT THE SECURITY PLATFORM TEAM

The Infrastructure Security team provides and supports the primitives that enable engineering to securely build applications and meet compliance obligations, while abstracting away the underlying complexity for the best possible developer experience.

Our work centers on workload identity and authorization: how internal applications authenticate to each other and to the services they depend on, and how that access is granted and enforced. We're replacing static secrets with short-lived identity credentials, bringing identity-based authentication to the services engineers use every day, and unifying how authorization is managed across the company.

We're a platform engineering team with a security mission. We measure success by the security outcomes we enable and by how much engineers enjoy building on what we ship - the secure path should be the easiest path.

- A systems thinker. You reason carefully about bootstrapping, circular dependencies, availability, and failure modes, especially for infrastructure that everything else depends on.

- A pragmatic migrator. You know that shipping the primitive is half the job. You can drive adoption across many teams, meet them where they are, and retire the legacy path.

- A strong partner to engineering. You build trust with engineers by understanding their priorities and making security frictionless.

- Excited about AI. You're embracing AI and automation to scale platform work and reduce toil.

- Curious and humble. You ask the basic questions, enjoy untangling complex systems, and bring others along with you.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Build workload identity infrastructure. Make short-lived identity credentials a default part of every application's runtime environment, in partnership with application platform owners.

- Bring identity-based authentication to internal services. Work with the owners of major internal dependencies to support identity certificates, make them the golden path for newly onboarding applications, and drive migration of existing ones.

- Eliminate static secrets. Replace all static passwords and service tokens with short-lived identity credentials, and build identity-authenticated egress proxies and API abstractions that inject and automatically rotate managed secrets for the external dependencies that still require them.

- Unify authorization. Build a single interface and framework through which authorization policies are centrally managed and enforced.

QUALIFICATIONS

- Strong working knowledge of secrets management, fine-gr

title: Integrated Marketing Manager, AI Impact
description:
About the Team

Like every team at OpenAI, the Marketing team contributes to our broader mission of ensuring that artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We help people understand what AI makes possible through the experiences of the people, communities, and customers using it.

We work closely with Social, Community, Communications, Creative, Production, and other teams to bring those experiences to life. Our work connects human stories with integrated marketing programs that build understanding and inspiration with our key audience.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Integrated Marketing Manager to identify and curate the strongest proof points of AI’s impact-across people, communities, and society-and turn them into stories and programs that resonate.

You’ll be a builder and storyteller with the curiosity to uncover an extraordinary story and the initiative to make something of it. You’ll seek out people using AI in meaningful ways, build relationships, understand what has changed for them, and help them share their experiences in their own voices.

Working deeply with Social, Community, and Communications, you’ll shape stories together and build the programs, content, and distribution plans that help them travel. That could mean developing a recurring story series, bringing a community’s experience to a national audience, or turning a customer story into a program that invites others to participate.

You’ll combine strong editorial instincts with integrated marketing leadership, taking work from discovery and a clear brief through production, launch, and measurement. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable shaping an ambitious idea, facilitating a conversation with a story participant, and organizing the people and resources needed to bring a program to life.

In this role, you will:

- Find the strongest proof points: Proactively discover people, communities, and customers using AI in meaningful ways. Evaluate the evidence, human significance, and audience relevance behind each opportunity.

- Build alongside Social, Community, and Communications: Partner from the outset on story discovery, creative ideas, programming, and distribution. Align on a shared plan, clear roles, and the right moments to bring stories to audiences.

- Turn stories into programs: Create integrated campaigns, recurring content series, community activations, and partnerships that give strong stories a life beyond a single asset or launch.

- Connect national reach with local relevance: Adapt stories, formats, messengers, and programs to the audiences and communities they serve. Identify when a local story can resonate nationally and how a national program can become meaningful locally.

- Lead work from idea to delivery: Own briefs, creative development, production, timelines, budgets, partner coordination, launch, and optimization across social, owned, earned, experiential, community, and relevant paid channels.

- Champion craft and credibility: Partner with Creative, producers, and agencies to make distinctive, engaging content. Ground stories in demonstrated impact, bring technical ideas to life through human experiences, and represent participants accurately and thoughtfully.

- Build a repeatable approach: Develop a network of internal and external partners and a practical process for sourcing, prioritizing, developing, and sharing stories. Create formats and programs that can grow while leaving room to act on unexpected opportunities.

- Measure what resonates: Set clear goals for audience understanding, reach, engagement, sharing, and participation. Use results and feedback from audiences and participants to improve the stories, formats, and programs we build.

You will thrive in this role if you have:

- Relevant experience: 12+ years in integrated marketing, content or editorial strategy, customer storytelling, community marketing, or related fields, including significant experience leading complex campaigns and programs.

title: Principal Infrastructure Architect: Data Platform
description:
ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute. You’ll make things happen-fast.

As a Principal Infrastructure Architect on our Infrastructure Architecture team, you will be the architecture team's partner to ZoomInfo 's data engineering organization. Data engineering owns the platforms and the products built on them. You bring the infrastructure patterns, evaluation rigor, and cross-team alignment that help them build and run those platforms well on GCP.
This is a cloud architect seat with a data specialty. You bring the same cloud, Kubernetes, networking, and infrastructure-as-code foundation as the rest of the architecture team, plus enough hands-on depth in data systems to be credible with the engineers who run them.
The work breaks down four ways:

•
Patterns. You establish and maintain the paved-road patterns data teams build on: infrastructure as code, CI/CD for data jobs and pipelines, monitoring and alerting, performance, and cost. You keep them easy to consume and self-service.

•
Enablement and alignment. You help data teams adopt those patterns, review their designs, and work through hard infrastructure trade-offs with them.

•
Evaluation. You run POCs of new data technologies and vendor offerings as part of the procurement and technology-lifecycle process, and you write recommendations engineering leaders can act on.

•
Shared stewardship. You take a full share of the architecture team's general work: weekly architecture reviews across all domains, standards and ADRs, and infrastructure consulting for any team that needs it.

The data estate is broad. We don't expect deep experience across all of it. We expect real depth in some areas and the ability to build depth in others as the work demands. Patterns get adopted here through leadership and communication rather than positional authority. You'll write reference implementations, open the first PRs, and stay hands-on through enablement when a critical initiative calls for it.
What You'll Do

•
Establish infrastructure patterns for data workloads. Design and maintain reference patterns for provisioning and operating the data platforms ZoomInfo runs: streaming and messaging (Kafka/Confluent, Pub/Sub), operational databases (PostgreSQL/Cloud SQL, MongoDB), analytical stores (BigQuery, Snowflake), search (Elasticsearch/Solr), pipeline orchestration and processing (Apache Airflow/Cloud Composer, Dataflow/Apache Beam), and open table formats (Apache Iceberg). Ship them as Terraform modules, GitOps workflows, and documented standards that data teams can adopt without reinventing them.

•
Build the data paved road. Today's delivery tooling is application-centric. Define CI/CD and GitOps patterns for data jobs and pipelines, and partner with platform engineering and data engineering to make data delivery as safe and automated as application delivery.

•
Establish performance, cost, and observability patterns. Give data teams the patterns and guidance to run stores and pipelines efficiently (query and storage optimization, partitioning and clustering, tiering and retention, workload isolation, right-sizing) and the monitoring, alerting, and SLO practices that make performance and cost visible. Set the baseline patterns for backup, restore, and disaster recovery of data stores, including RTO/RPO targets. Partner with FinOps on data-layer spend. Review workloads with teams against these patterns and help them align.

•
Evaluate new technologies. Run structured POCs of emerging data technologies and vendor offerings as part of the procurement and technology-lifecycle process. Recent examples include graph and distributed SQL databases, stream processing (Apache Flink, Confluent Flink), and schema management and catalo

title: Product Manager (US Cards)
description:
ABOUT LENDABLE

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

- One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

- Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

- Profitable since 2017

- Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

- Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/lendable.co.uk)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

JOIN US IF YOU WANT TO

1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

In six years, Lendable has built a profitable, market-leading credit card in the UK. In 2023, we brought that playbook to the US and set an even higher bar. This year the US credit card business scaled rapidly: our run rate grew more than 20x in the last six months.

A lot of the work of getting customers through the door is in place. The next stage is about what happens once they’re in: helping them pay on time, giving more credit to the ones who earn it, getting people back on track when they fall behind, and ensuring an intuitive user experience across channels.

If you're excited by fintech, lending and scaling products in a fast-moving environment, this role offers real ownership, impact and room to grow.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Product Manager to join the product team, and will cover post booking areas including payments, collections, credit limit increases, spend, and the mobile app.

No two weeks look the same. One week you might be sizing an opportunity, the next week sitting with the ops team to understand why customers are calling, or putting a rough version of an idea in front of real customers before anyone builds the proper one. We care more about how quickly we learn than how polished the first attempt looks.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

- Running experiments across the customer lifecycle, such as how and when we remind people to pay, what gets them to set up autopay, and how we gamify engagement

- Working with credit risk and data science on how to apply models to new use cases and opportunities

- Finding cheap, fast ways to test an idea (a manual process, an email, a script) with AI before committing engineering time to it

- Gathering customer research to get truthful and unbiased reads

- Building tools and automations with AI that save time for you, the ops team and the wider business

- Doing whatever it takes to get something live, including the unglamorous parts like unblocking developers, socializing with legal and compliance, or writing the guide for the ops team

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Don’t worry if you don’t meet all these criteria. We'd love to talk to any great candidate that is excited, inquisitive, and a go-getter.

- 1-4 years in product, strategy, analytics, consulting or operations, with some time spent working closely to product or execution teams to deliver value

- You ask a lot of questions and you're not satisfied until you understand why something is happening

- You enjoy forming a hypothesis and finding the quickest way to test it, even if the first version is rough

- You'

We're AWeber , a remote‑first company that helps small businesses around the world form meaningful connections with their customers and grow their businesses using our marketing communication software. We are fanatical about small businesses and we hope you are too!

At AWeber , agentic development is core to how we build. Our engineers spend most of their time designing agents and agentic engineering systems, reviewing agent‑generated work for quality and correctness, and coordinating that work across the codebase. As an Engineering Team Lead, you build a small team of engineers who do exactly that into a high‑performing, healthy, well‑functioning group, and you lead them from inside the work.

We are looking for the senior engineer other people already rely on, who leads and grows a team without losing their own hands on the keyboard. Your mission is to help a capable, curious group ship work the org can trust, move quickly without cutting corners, and consistently finish what they start.

On any given day, you could be found reviewing an agent‑generated pull request on a risky path and coaching the engineer on how they verified it, running a 1:1 that turns someone's recurring frustration into an owned initiative, interviewing a candidate and sharpening how your team evaluates new hires, pairing for an hour to unblock a stalled migration, deciding what comes off the plate so your team is not underwater, or carrying your team's priorities into a cross‑team engineering forum.

• Make people decisions and difficult trade‑offs with care, and own the outcomes.

• Establish standards and inspire others, not just through your own expertise but through mentorship and advocacy.

• Default to open, transparent communication, and adapt your message to engineers, peers, product partners, and leadership.

• Stay calm and steady when priorities compete, and keep your team oriented on what matters most.

• Stay a forever learner, and grow the people around you.

• Demonstrated ability to design solutions with AI development tools and coding assistants, and to raise a team's standard for reviewing agent‑generated work.

• Strong experience across our stack: Python, React, and TypeScript, plus databases, caching strategies, UNIX development tools, and deploying to AWS or other cloud infrastructure.

Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Full Time Clinician (Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant) to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.
You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.
Job highlights
The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.
In this role, you will:

• Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

• Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

• Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

• Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

• Conduct virtual visits as needed

• Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

​
A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.

We're not your average benefits platform - we're the driving force that uplifts people's lives. Our technology connects the entire benefits ecosystem, creating better outcomes for employers, employees, brokers, and providers.

Our mission is clear: to build a world where everything works at its best, ensuring every employee gets the support they need to thrive-both at work and beyond.

YOUR MISSION

As our Head of Implementation, you will build the foundations that let implementation scale: the operating model, the process and the standards we need to grow well beyond where we are today. Enterprise implementation is slow and manual almost everywhere, so you will rebuild ours around agents, which almost no delivery leader gets the chance to do on live enterprise builds. Through all of it, you own how our largest customers experience Ben, from the enterprise sales conversation through to a confident go-live.

- Transform how we implement enterprise customers: today we deliver well on the strength of the people doing it, and that ceiling is now the thing holding us back. Rebuild the operating model, the standards and the reusable components so we can take on far more without adding a person for every customer, and collapse the time it takes a customer to reach value.

- Make implementation AI-native: our builds are technically complex (integrations, eligibility logic, huge volumes of data). Decide what agents can genuinely own, where humans stay in the loop, then rebuild delivery around that. We expect a function where your team's time goes on judgement and relationships while the repeatable work runs itself.

- Lead the team through the change: you will lead 8 to 10 Implementation Managers through a transformation of how they work. Bring them with you, develop the people already leading within the team, and build the bench that lets this function keep growing.

- Make the wider business faster because of you: partner with commercial, customer and product leaders so the journey joins up before, during and after a build, and so what your team learns changes what we sell and what we build.

description:
bunch https://www.bunch.capital/ is building the backbone of private markets. We are enabling next-gen fund operations with one integrated system that combines secure data infrastructure, AI-powered workflows and expert fund services. If you value ownership, growth through real responsibility, and working with a thoughtful, ambitious team, this role might be for you.

YOUR ROLE

As a Senior or Staff-level Product Manager for Growth at bunch, you will lead a small Growth squad focused on discovering, validating, and shipping products that open the upmarket segment - larger VC funds and private equity managers whose scale and complexity put them beyond today’s product, but who become our most valuable customers the moment we can serve them.

This is greenfield work. You’ll start from real conversations with target accounts, not an inherited roadmap.

You will:

- Own the Growth squad end to end: discovery, roadmap, build, and commercial outcomes

- Work closely with Commercial to identify target accounts worth winning, then get in front of them through discovery calls, demos, and POC scoping

- Identify recurring problems across upmarket accounts and decide what to build to deliver the highest ROI

- Prototype fast - with the team and with AI tooling - so an idea becomes something a prospect can touch in weeks or months, not quarters

- Run experiments knowing most will fail: kill the losers quickly and cheaply, and double down on what converts

- Convert working prototypes into paid POCs, and paid POCs into signed contracts and product lines

- Lead a small team of engineers as an active, hands-on product manager

About you

- 7+ years in product, with a track record of taking ambiguous, zero-to-one problems to shipped, revenue-generating products

- Experience operating at senior or staff level, with the ability to run a squad without someone setting direction for you

- Strong fintech experience and comfort with financial services complexity, regulation, and sophisticated buyers

- Commercial mindset: you think in business cases and ROI, can hold your own in front of a fund CFO or COO, and understand how discovery turns into POCs and signed contracts

- Fluent with AI tools such as Claude, Lovable, or similar, especially for research, analysis, and prototyping

- Experimental by temperament: energised by high-risk, high-reward work and able to design experiments so failures are fast and cheap

- Comfortable with ambiguity and small teams; you would rather own one hard problem with two people than manage twenty on a roadmap someone else set

- Exposure to private markets - VC, PE, fund administration, or working inside a GP or fund - is a plus

- Experience in a growth, new-ventures, or incubation function is a plus

Success Indicators

- A visible pipeline of experiments run, killed, or scaled, with clear reasoning for each

- Paid MVPs landed with accounts previously out of reach

- MVPs with a clear path to signed contracts in the upmarket segment

Workplace & Benefits

- Customizable benefits package (wellbeing, sport, mobility, food, and more)

- 28 days of vacation, plus 2 company days and local public holidays

- Remote work with quarterly trips to Berlin or elsewhere in Europe.

- A great tech and work setup

- Work with a diverse team of 120+ bunchies from 40+ countries, with leaders who are best-in-class in their domains

Hiring process

1. People Team Interview (30 min) - Meet us & check initial fit

2. Hiring Manager Interview (60 min) - Collaboration, ownership, and product/commercial fit

3. Product Case Interview (60 min) - Problem discovery, experimentation, and prioritisation

4. Cross-functional Interview (60 min) - Commercial collaboration, stakeholder management, and impact

5. Final Round (60 min) - Meet senior leaders from Product and Commercial

Optional Meet & Greet (30 min) - Meet your future teammates

title: Regional Director of Pooled Customer Success
description:
ABOUT CODERABBIT

CodeRabbit is the leading AI code review platform, trusted by more than 17,000 customers and 150,000 open-source projects, conducting over 2 million code reviews each week. We build the symbiotic partnership between developers and AI that makes shipping fast software safe again, reviewing every pull request, IDE change, and CLI commit so teams can move quickly without breaking things.

 

We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation - building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.

Location: San Francisco, Hybrid

ABOUT THE TEAM

CodeRabbit is the AI code review platform. Development teams install it on their repositories and it reviews every pull request, so it sits in the daily workflow of a large and fast-growing customer base. The Scaled Success team is responsible for the health of that base. It is a team of a program manager, a content and enablement specialist, a success analytics engineer and a success operations manager, reporting to the Director of Scaled Success. The pooled customer success team is the next team to be added, and this role leads it.

THE ROLE

You build and run the pooled customer success team. Work arrives on a shared queue when a signal fires: onboarding has stalled, nothing has been configured, the only active user has gone quiet, a renewal is approaching, a cancellation has been started, or a team is using fewer seats than it has bought. The signals come from our configuration maturity model, which scores every account on how deeply it has set up the product, and from the automated campaigns that escalate when a customer needs a person.

You design the queue, write the routing rules, set the response standards, build the playbooks, hire the team, and measure whether the motion holds retention in the band it covers. You work directly with the Director, the Scaled Success program manager, the Success Analytics Engineer and the Content and Enablement Specialist.

This team runs on signals, and the help arrives when the customer needs it. The person who builds it will learn how to run customer success this way from the inside, and will have the data to show what works.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

- Hiring and managing the pooled customer success managers, starting with the first hires in your first quarter

- Queue design: which signals create work, how work is prioritized, the response and resolution standards, and how a case closes

- The routing rules between the digital, pooled and named lanes, including the escalation path out of digital and the hand-back when an account grows into named coverage

- The playbook library, one per trigger: what a CSM does on a dormant account, a solo user, a stalled onboarding, a cancellation notice, an approaching renewal. Written with the Content and Enablement Specialist and kept current from what the queue teaches you

- The save lane: cancellation and non-renewal signals routed to a person, the reason captured on every one, and the fixable ones fixed

- The expansion hand-off: when the team surfaces seat headroom or a buying signal, the account goes to the account executive working the scaled lanes, with the context they need to close

- The team's readout: queue volume by trigger, time to first response, time to resolution, configuration movement, and retention of covered accounts, built with the Success Analytics Engineer and read monthly

- Capacity: how many accounts one person on the queue can carry, measured from the queue, and the case for extending pooled coverage further down the base as triggers and playbooks mature

YOUR FIRST QUARTER

- Hire the first pooled customer success managers

- Define the trigger set, the response standard for each trigger, and get the queue live i
